Buscamos personas curiosas, comprometidas y con ganas de aprender, colaborar y crear soluciones de impacto real.
summary:
Anomaly Zero is an interactive, NASA-powered Earth science exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the challenge of understanding how Earth's environmental systems change and interact by bringing multiple NASA datasets into one accessible interface.

Using NASA's MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, and GLDAS products, Anomaly Zero enables users to explore air temperature, precipitation, and soil moisture through monthly time-series visualizations, interactive maps, and transparent data provenance.

Our initial prototype focuses on exploratory observations from 2005 in southeastern Australia, using the Murray–Darling Basin as a geographic reference.

Unlike conventional dashboards, Anomaly Zero emphasizes scientific transparency: users can distinguish authentic observations from demonstration data, inspect data quality limitations, and understand the spatial and temporal constraints of each dataset.

By making complex Earth observation data easier to explore and interpret, we aim to support scientific curiosity, environmental education, and future evidence-based investigations into Earth's interconnected systems.
details:
Anomaly Zero — Exploring Earth's Connected Systems

The Problem

Understanding Earth's interconnected systems requires analyzing environmental variables from multiple scientific datasets. However, NASA Earth observation products differ in spatial resolution, temporal coverage, measurement units, and quality conventions. These differences make it challenging for students, researchers, and the public to explore environmental changes and understand how different datasets relate to one another.

Our Solution

Anomaly Zero is an interactive web application that brings together authentic NASA Earth science observations in an accessible, transparent, and reproducible exploration environment.

Our prototype uses the Murray–Darling Basin in southeastern Australia as a geographic reference and explores monthly observations from 2005 across three NASA products:

  • MERRA-2: Near-surface air temperature at 2 meters (T2M), measured in Kelvin.
  • GPM IMERG: Monthly mean precipitation rate, measured in mm/hr.
  • GLDAS Noah: Modeled surface soil moisture at a depth of 0–10 cm, measured in kg/m².

The application allows users to select products, observation sites, and time periods; inspect monthly time-series charts; compare variables through independently scaled visualizations; explore geographic context using an interactive map; and export available observations as CSV files.

Technology and Implementation

Anomaly Zero was developed using Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, Docker, MapLibre GL JS, and scientific data-processing tools.

The backend serves structured environmental observations through documented API endpoints, while the frontend presents the results through interactive charts, tables, geographic visualization, and contextual information.

The project incorporates NASA Earthdata products and reproducible derived datasets, including source identifiers, units, coordinates, and provenance information.

Scientific Transparency

A central principle of Anomaly Zero is to avoid presenting exploratory observations as scientifically validated conclusions.

Our initial observations represent candidate sampling locations, not approved regional averages. Different NASA products have different spatial footprints, and provider quality assurance has not been fully evaluated.

Therefore, the prototype does not claim statistically significant correlations, causal relationships, long-term climate trends, or validated regional anomalies.

We explicitly distinguish authentic derived observations from synthetic demonstration data and communicate the limitations of our analyses.

Innovation and Impact

Rather than simply plotting environmental measurements, Anomaly Zero combines NASA datasets with interactive exploration and transparent scientific metadata.

Our goal is to make Earth science more approachable while encouraging responsible interpretation of environmental information.

The platform establishes a foundation for future spatial alignment, statistically validated multivariable analysis, georeferenced NASA imagery, and expanded historical observations.

Anomaly Zero demonstrates how accessible software and open Earth observation data can help users investigate our planet while respecting scientific uncertainty.
